about: Groups 2 and 3 of the benchmark corpus (lib/benchmark/README.md). Each case is a claim the tool checks and Reference.java checks on a JVM, apart from the tool: its expected answer, the source it comes from, why it holds or fails, and, for a violation, an input on which the JVM refutes it.

cases.source: JDK-5045582; Joshua Bloch, "Extra, Extra - Read All About It: Nearly All Binary Searches and Mergesorts are Broken", Google Research blog, 2 June 2006
cases.why: low + high overflows once it passes Integer.MAX_VALUE, and the quotient of the negative sum is below low

cases.source: JDK-5045582; Joshua Bloch, "Extra, Extra - Read All About It: Nearly All Binary Searches and Mergesorts are Broken", Google Research blog, 2 June 2006
cases.why: the sum of two non-negative ints fits 32 bits unsigned, and >>> 1 halves it as unsigned

cases.source: JDK-5045582; Joshua Bloch, "Extra, Extra - Read All About It: Nearly All Binary Searches and Mergesorts are Broken", Google Research blog, 2 June 2006
cases.why: the fix changes the midpoint only where low + high overflows, or outside the search's ranges

cases.source: JDK-5045582; Joshua Bloch, "Extra, Extra - Read All About It: Nearly All Binary Searches and Mergesorts are Broken", Google Research blog, 2 June 2006
cases.why: the overflow needs low + high > Integer.MAX_VALUE, an array of more than 2^30 elements: on arrays of up to 8 elements, the domain of the proof, the two searches agree. The bug is real and outside the domain

cases.source: FindBugs bug pattern RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_HASHCODE, "Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed 32-bit hashcode"
cases.why: Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is Integer.MIN_VALUE, whose remainder by 3 is -2

cases.source: FindBugs bug pattern RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_HASHCODE, "Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed 32-bit hashcode"
cases.why: hash & 0x7fffffff is non-negative, and so is its remainder by a positive count, which is below the count

cases.source: FindBugs bug pattern RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_HASHCODE, "Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed 32-bit hashcode"
cases.why: for a non-negative hash, Math.abs(hash) and hash & 0x7fffffff are the hash

cases.source: The CERT Oracle Coding Standard for Java, NUM00-J, "Detect or prevent integer overflow"; JDK 8's java.io.OutputStream.write(byte[], int, int) also tests (off + len) < 0
cases.why: off + len overflows to a negative number, which passes the check, and the loop runs no iteration: 0 for a range that is not in the array

cases.source: written for the benchmark on 2026-11-06, after the engines' optimizations, and not changed to suit them
cases.why: a + b overflows exactly when both operands' signs differ from the wrapped sum's, and then saturates toward a's sign

cases.source: written for the benchmark on 2026-11-06, after the engines' optimizations, and not changed to suit them
cases.why: a + b == 2 * (a & b) + (a ^ b), so the floor of half the sum is (a & b) + ((a ^ b) >> 1), with no overflow

cases.source: written for the benchmark on 2026-11-06, after the engines' optimizations, and not changed to suit them
cases.why: (a + b) >>> 1 shifts the sign bit in: the mean of -1 and -1 comes out as Integer.MAX_VALUE
